    - text: CLASS 12 · PROBABILITY
    - heading "Independent Events" [level=1]
    - paragraph: Knowing one event does not change the probability of the other.
    - text: 18 min · ADVANCED · CONCEPT · independence
    - navigation "Lesson sections":
      - button "Test"
      - button "Outcome Grid"
      - button "Simulation"
      - button "Rule"
      - button "Practice"
      - button "Reset lab":
        - img
        - text: Reset lab
    - article:
      - heading "DUAL EXPERIMENT" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Flip a fair coin and roll a fair six-sided die. Each outcome is equally likely.
      - heading "COIN" [level=3]
      - text: H Fair coin
      - heading "DIE" [level=3]
      - img
      - text: Fair six-sided die
      - button "Flip Coin"
      - button "Roll Die":
        - img
        - text: Roll Die
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Last result: Heads"
        - img
        - text: "4"
    - article:
      - heading "SELECT EVENTS" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Choose event A from the coin and event B from the die.
      - text: Event A (Coin)
      - combobox "Coin event A":
        - option "A = Heads (H)" [selected]
        - option "A = Tails (T)"
        - option "A = Heads or Tails"
      - paragraph: P(A) = 6/12 = 0.5
      - text: Event B (Die)
      - combobox "Die event B":
        - option "B = Even (2, 4, 6)" [selected]
        - option "B = Odd (1, 3, 5)"
        - option "B = Prime (2, 3, 5)"
        - option "B = Six (6)"
        - option "B = Greater than 3 (4, 5, 6)"
        - option "B = Any face (1–6)"
      - paragraph: P(B) = 6/12 = 0.5
    - article:
      - heading "PROBABILITY SUMMARY" [level=2]
      - paragraph: P(A ∩ B) = 3/12 = 0.25
      - paragraph: P(A)P(B) = 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B)
      - strong: Events A and B are independent.
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: Independence means knowing one event does not change the probability of the other.
    - heading "OUTCOME GRID (12 EQUALLY LIKELY OUTCOMES)" [level=2]
    - table:
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Coin (A) / Die (B) 1 2 (B) 3 4 (B) 5 6 (B)":
          - columnheader "Coin (A) / Die (B)"
          - columnheader "1"
          - columnheader "2 (B)"
          - columnheader "3"
          - columnheader "4 (B)"
          - columnheader "5"
          - columnheader "6 (B)"
      - rowgroup:
        - row "H (A) H, 1 H, 2, favorable H, 3 H, 4, favorable, last result H, 5 H, 6, favorable":
          - rowheader "H (A)"
          - cell "H, 1": (H, 1)
          - cell "H, 2, favorable": (H, 2)
          - cell "H, 3": (H, 3)
          - cell "H, 4, favorable, last result": (H, 4)
          - cell "H, 5": (H, 5)
          - cell "H, 6, favorable": (H, 6)
        - row "T (not A) T, 1 T, 2 T, 3 T, 4 T, 5 T, 6":
          - rowheader "T (not A)"
          - cell "T, 1": (T, 1)
          - cell "T, 2": (T, 2)
          - cell "T, 3": (T, 3)
          - cell "T, 4": (T, 4)
          - cell "T, 5": (T, 5)
          - cell "T, 6": (T, 6)
    - paragraph: "Favorable for A ∩ B (3 outcomes): (H, 2), (H, 4), (H, 6) Total outcomes = 12"
    - article:
      - heading "LIVE INDEPENDENCE CHECK" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Two equivalent tests must both be true.
      - 'heading "Test 1: Product rule" [level=3]':
        - img
        - text: "Test 1: Product rule"
      - paragraph: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B) 0.25 = 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25
      - 'heading "Test 2: Conditioning" [level=3]':
        - img
        - text: "Test 2: Conditioning"
      - paragraph: P(B | A) = P(B) 0.5 = 0.5
    - article:
      - 'heading "REVEAL: KNOWING A = HEADS" [level=2]'
      - paragraph: Given heads, the remaining die outcomes are still equally likely.
      - paragraph: P(B | A) = 3/6 = 0.5 = P(B)
      - heading "Probability of B (Even (2, 4, 6)) on the die" [level=3]
      - text: Before knowing A
      - progressbar
      - text: 0.5 After knowing A (Heads)
      - progressbar
      - text: "0.5"
      - paragraph: The probability does not change. B is unaffected by A.
    - article:
      - heading "SIMULATION (FREQUENCY OF A ∩ B)" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Run more trials to see frequencies approach 0.25.
      - button "Run 1"
      - button "Run 100"
      - button "Run 1000"
      - button "Auto":
        - img
        - text: Auto
      - table:
        - rowgroup:
          - row "Trials Hits (A ∩ B) Frequency Expected":
            - columnheader "Trials"
            - columnheader "Hits (A ∩ B)"
            - columnheader "Frequency"
            - columnheader "Expected"
        - rowgroup:
          - row "No trials yet":
            - cell "No trials yet"
      - paragraph: Theoretical probability is distinct from observed frequency.
    - article:
      - 'heading "COMPARE: INDEPENDENT vs DEPENDENT" [level=2]'
      - paragraph: Switch the experiment to see how probabilities change.
      - button "Independent (Coin & Die)" [pressed]
      - button "Dependent (2R, 1B balls)"
      - paragraph: "Fair coin and fair die: separate independent experiments."
      - table:
        - rowgroup:
          - row "Event Before knowing A After knowing A":
            - columnheader "Event"
            - columnheader "Before knowing A"
            - columnheader "After knowing A"
        - rowgroup:
          - 'row "B: Even (2, 4, 6) 0.5 0.5"':
            - 'cell "B: Even (2, 4, 6)"'
            - cell "0.5"
            - cell "0.5"
      - paragraph: Knowing heads does not change the die probabilities.
    - article:
      - heading "INDEPENDENCE vs MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE" [level=2]
      - heading "Independent Events" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Knowing one does not change the probability of the other.
      - paragraph: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B)
      - paragraph: "Example: coin and die."
      - heading "Mutually Exclusive Events" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Cannot happen at the same time.
      - paragraph: P(A ∩ B) = 0
      - paragraph: For two positive-probability events, this rules out independence.
    - article:
      - heading "COMMON MISCONCEPTION" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: COMMON MISCONCEPTION
      - paragraph: Do not confuse independence with mutual exclusivity.
      - paragraph: "Rolling a die: A = Even, B = Odd."
      - paragraph: They cannot occur together. P(A ∩ B) = 0, but P(A)P(B) = 1/4. They are not independent!
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: A box has 5 red and 7 blue balls. Draw twice with replacement. Let A = first red, B = second blue.
      - paragraph: P(A) = 5/12, P(B) = 7/12 P(A ∩ B) = 35/144 P(A)P(B) = (5/12)(7/12) = 35/144
      - paragraph: Since P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B), A and B are independent.
